REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">THOMASVILLE, Ga., November 12, 2026 &#x2013; Flowers Foods, Inc. (NYSE: FLO) today reported financial results for the company&#x2019;s 12-week third quarter ended October 10, 2026.</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> </font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline solid;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Third Quarter Summary:</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Compared to the prior year third quarter where applicable</font></p><div class="item-list-element-wrapper" style="margin-left:4.528%;tab-size:32px;display:flex;font-size:6.03pt;margin-top:6pt;justify-content:flex-start;font-family:Times New style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Net sales</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;vertical-align:super;font-size:6.03pt;line-height:1.5;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">(1)</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> decreased 4.7% to $1.169 billion as favorable price/mix was more than offset by lower volume.</font></div></div><div class="item-list-element-wrapper" style="margin-left:4.528%;tab-size:32px;display:flex;font-size:6.03pt;margin-top:6pt;justify-content:flex-start;font-family:Times New style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Net income decreased 63.6% to $14.4 million, representing 1.2% of sales, a 200-basis point decrease, primarily due to lower sales volume, increased marketing investment, higher logistics costs, and greater outside purchases of product. These factors were partially offset by lower incentive compensation, lower ingredient costs, and lower distributor distribution fees. Adjusted net income</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;vertical-align:super;font-size:6.03pt;line-height:1.5;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">(2)</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> decreased 56.0% to $21.4 million.</font></div></div><div class="item-list-element-wrapper" style="margin-left:4.528%;tab-size:32px;display:flex;font-size:6.03pt;margin-top:6pt;justify-content:flex-start;font-family:Times New Roman;align-items:baseline;margin-bottom:0;min-width:4.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;vertical-align:super;font-size:6.03pt;line-height:1.5;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">(2)</font><font 280-basis point decrease.</font></div></div><div class="item-list-element-wrapper" style="margin-left:4.528%;tab-size:32px;display:flex;font-size:6.03pt;margin-top:6pt;justify-content:flex-start;font-family:Times New Adjusted diluted EPS</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;vertical-align:super;font-size:6.03pt;line-height:1.5;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">(2)</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> decreased $0.13 to $0.10.<br> </font></div></div><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline solid;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Chairman and CEO Remarks:<br></font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline solid;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">&#160;</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#262626;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">&#x201c;Our third-quarter results reflect a continued challenging operating environment, driven by pressure on household budgets, evolving consumer behavior and heightened promotional activity, as well as areas where we need to move faster with focused execution,&#x201d; said Ryals McMullian, chairman and CEO of Flowers Foods. &#x201c;Following the second quarter, we expected our earlier pricing actions and the relaunch of Nature's Own with fewer, simpler ingredients to help stabilize performance as we worked to introduce new innovation to market. We are seeing encouraging signs for Nature&#x2019;s Own, including improving sequential trends and growing awareness of the relaunch, although the pace of improvement has been slower than anticipated, primarily in loaf, where category trends remain challenging. We are accelerating actions already underway to strengthen customer execution, close innovation gaps, and better align our portfolio with evolving consumer preferences.&#x201d;</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#262626;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> </font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#262626;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">&#x201c;While it will take time for our initiatives to translate more fully into results, we believe they are putting Flowers on a stronger path forward. We expect the environment to remain challenging in the near term, but we remain confident in the long-term potential of the business. We participate in large, attractive markets across fresh packaged bread, cake, better-for-you snacking, and foodservice, and our leading brands, extensive network, and deep customer relationships provide a strong foundation to drive improved performance and long-term growth. Given our third-quarter performance and current conditions, we are adjusting our 2026 guidance.&#x201d;</font><font style="color:#262626;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> </font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline solid;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Revised Outlook: 52-week Fiscal 2026, the Company Expects:</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">&#160;</font></p><div class="item-list-element-wrapper" style="margin-left:4.528%;tab-size:32px;display:flex;font-size:9pt;margin-top:6pt;justify-content:flex-start;font-family:Times New Roman;align-items:baseline;margin-bottom:0;min-width:4.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:4.7521786492374725%;word-break:keep-all;display:inline-flex;justify-content:flex-start;">&#x2022;</font><div style="display:inline;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Net sales of approximately $5.016 billion to $5.063 billion, representing a -4.6% to -3.7% change compared to the prior year. Prior guidance called for net sales of approximately $5.070 billion to $5.142 billion. </font></div></div><div class="item-list-element-wrapper" (l) disruptions in our direct-store-delivery distribution model, including litigation or an adverse ruling by a court or regulatory or governmental body that could affect the independent contractor classifications of the independent distributor partners (&#x201c;IDPs&#x201d;), and changes to our direct-store-delivery distribution model in California, (m) increasing legal complexity and legal proceedings that we are or may become subject to, (n) labor shortages and turnover or increases in employee and employee-related costs, (o) impacts from credit rating agency downgrades and our ability to satisfy financial covenants in our credit facility and term loan facility, which could have an adverse effect on our costs and availability of capital; (p) risks related to our indebtedness and current leverage profile; (q) the credit, business, and legal risks associated with IDPs and customers, which operate in the highly competitive retail food and foodservice industries, (r) any business disruptions due to political instability, pandemics, armed hostilities, incidents of terrorism, natural disasters, labor strikes or work stoppages, technological breakdowns, product contamination, product recalls or safety concerns related to our products, or the responses to or repercussions from any of these or similar events or conditions and our ability to insure against such events, (s) the failure of our information technology systems to perform adequately, including any interruptions, intrusions, cyber-attacks or security breaches of such systems or risks associated with the implementation of the upgrade of our ERP system; and (t) the potential impact of climate change on the company, including physical and transition risks, our availability or restriction of resources, higher regulatory and compliance costs, reputational risks, and our availability of capital on attractive terms. The foregoing list of important factors does not include all such factors, nor does it necessarily present them in order of importance. In addition, you should consult other disclosures made by the company (such as in our other filings with the SEC or in company press releases) for other factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from those projected by the company. Refer to Part I, Item 1A., Risk Factors, of our Form 10-K, Part II, Item 1A., Risk Factors, of the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 10, 2026 and subsequent filings with the SEC for additional information regarding factors that could affect the company&#x2019;s results of operations, financial condition and liquidity.   <div class="main-content-container" style="z-index:5;position:relative;"><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:8pt;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">obligation to publicly revise or update such statements, except as required by law. You are advised, however, to consult any further public disclosures by the company (such as in our filings with the SEC or in company press releases) on related subjects.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline solid;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Information Regarding Non-GAAP Financial Measures</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">The company prepares its consolidated financial statements in accordance with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP). However, from time to time, the company may present in its public statements, press releases and SEC filings, non-GAAP financial measures such as, EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA margin, adjusted net income, adjusted diluted EPS, adjusted income tax expense, adjusted selling, distribution and administrative expenses (SD&amp;A), and gross margin excluding depreciation and amortization. The company&#x2019;s definitions of these non-GAAP measures may differ from similarly titled measures used by others. These non-GAAP measures should be considered supplemental to, and not a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">The company defines EBITDA as earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. Earnings are net income. The company believes that EBITDA is a useful tool for managing the operations of its business and is an indicator of the company&#x2019;s ability to incur and service indebtedness and generate free cash flow. The company also believes that EBITDA measures are commonly reported and widely used by investors and other interested parties as measures of a company&#x2019;s operating performance and debt servicing ability because EBITDA measures assist in comparing performance on a consistent basis without regard to depreciation or amortization, which can vary significantly depending upon accounting methods and non-operating factors (such as historical cost). EBITDA is also a widely-accepted financial indicator of a company&#x2019;s ability to incur and service indebtedness.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">EBITDA should not be considered an alternative to (a) income from operations or net income (loss) as a measure of operating performance; (b) cash flows provided by operating, investing and financing activities (as determined in accordance with GAAP) as a measure of the company&#x2019;s ability to meet its cash needs; or (c) any other indicator of performance or liquidity that has been determined in accordance with GAAP.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">The company defines adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA margin, adjusted net income, adjusted diluted EPS, adjusted income tax expense and adjusted SD&amp;A, respectively, to exclude additional costs that the company considers important to present to investors to increase the investors&#x2019; insights about the company&#x2019;s core operations. These costs include, but are not limited to, the costs of closing a plant or costs associated with acquisition and integration-related activities, restructuring activities, certain impairment charges, legal settlements, costs to implement an enterprise resource planning system and enhance bakery digital capabilities (business process improvement costs) to provide investors direct insight into these costs, and other costs impacting past and future comparability. The company believes that these measures, when considered together with its GAAP financial results, provide management and investors with a more complete understanding of its business operating results, including underlying trends, by excluding the effects of certain charges. Adjusted EBITDA is used as a performance measure in the company&#x2019;s incentive compensation program.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Presentation of gross margin includes depreciation and amortization in the materials, supplies, labor and other production costs according to GAAP. Our method of presenting gross margin excludes the depreciation and amortization components, as discussed above.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">The reconciliations attached provide reconciliations of the non-GAAP measures used in this release to the most comparable GAAP financial measure.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:10pt;margin-top:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">&#160;</font></p></div>
